artigo.texto: Virginia Gov. Abigail Spanberger signed an executive order Sept. 18 to lay out the state’s new plan to establish environmental protections and ensure transparency around data centers. Virginia has become the “data center capital of the world.” That has brought tax revenue and jobs for localities but also immense energy demand. And environmentalists worry about the industry’s impact on water supply and air quality. Earlier this summer, lawmakers added a tax in the state budget for the energy data centers use. Spanberger also supported budget language that requires new data centers in “cooling-water scarcity areas” to minimize how much water they use to cool their servers. The order bans any employees under the governor’s supervision from signing non-disclosure disagreements, which can lead to data center projects being approved at the local level without public input. The governor’s office will make a toolkit for local leaders that includes the questions they need to ask data center development companies, a community benefits agreement template and recommendations for siting projects in ways that minimize community impacts. The order directs the state Department of Environmental Quality to submit a study by March 17, 2027, that evaluates the cumulative impact of emissions from backup diesel generators at data centers. It also prevents the Virginia Economic Development Partnership from helping to expedite permits for facilities that need more than 25 megawatts of power. The executive order is part of the governor’s Data Center Accountability Framework. The framework lists priorities for the 2027 legislative session such as establishing standards for energy efficiency, water use, land impacts and the decommissioning of data centers. Spanberger plans to limit the amount of energy that data centers can generate from on-site natural gas operations. As for facilities fighting to get on the grid, they could connect first if they reduce generator emissions by 60% or bring clean energy five years faster than the Virginia Clean Economy Act requires. Labor unions have pushed against policies that would make data centers leave Virginia, taking maintenance and construction jobs with them. Michael Town, executive director of the Virginia League of Conservation Voters, said Virginia isn’t kicking the industry out, but they must be good neighbors if they want to stay. “If done right, there is a path for continued job creation, responsible investment and clean energy deployment that protects ratepayers and delivers benefits for families and communities,” said Nicole Riley, director of Virginia government affairs for the Data Center Coalition. Environmentalists are split on the policy, with some saying it doesn’t go far enough. The Piedmont Environmental Council wants Spanberger to call for a special session and to enact a statewide moratorium, a decision New York Gov. Kathy Hochul took in July. “The industry has operated without sufficient oversight and accountability for far too long,” the council said in a statement. “Communities need a pause and real protection, not just a framework to guide the 2027 legislative process.”

Preface: Price Signals and Industry Stage This week (September 18–24, 2026), SMM solid-state battery material prices remained weak, with pressure concentrated in the sulfide segment. LPSC averaged RMB 3,400/kg; battery-grade lithium sulfide was RMB 1.3 million/t, but still far from the RMB 500,000/t cost target—this is the core contradiction. Oxide LATP and LLZO held steady at RMB 99/kg and RMB 630/kg, respectively. Anode silicon-carbon (resin-based/bio-based) held at RMB 525,000/t and RMB 298,000/t; lithium metal held steady. Cathode high-nickel ternary materials weakened overall: 8-series fell within the RMB 180,000–190,000/t range, 9-series consumer-grade fell to RMB 188,000/t, and the premium for solid-state-specific cathodes has not yet become independent. New quotes for lithium-rich manganese-based materials were added, but transactions await verification. This week, SMM announced that starting September 29, it will add four price points: lithium-rich manganese-based materials (high, medium, and low voltage), hydrogen sulfide, and nano titanium dioxide, covering three key links: solid-state battery cathode materials, sulfide electrolyte precursors, and oxide electrolyte raw materials. The expansion of this pricing system is itself a signal: more solid-state battery materials are moving from “lab” to a “quotable, tradable” stage, but most varieties remain in small-batch or pilot stages. Public transactions are sparse, and the reliability of price signals is limited. Core judgment: The core contradiction on the price side is not in the cathode or anode, but in lithium sulfide. The current battery-grade lithium sulfide price of RMB 1.3 million/t is still four times away from Gotion High-tech’s cost target of “lithium sulfide down to RMB 500,000/t and solid electrolyte down to RMB 300,000/t, entering the RMB 1/Wh era.” Several developments in this week’s documents—Sinocera’s sulfide electrolyte automated production line completed, Tengyuan Cobalt and Hunan Liuli jointly building a lithium sulfide pilot line—point precisely to attacking this bottleneck. II. Materials: Cathode, Anode, Electrolyte 2.1 Electrolyte: Sulfide Production Lines Completed in Clusters; Oxide Thousand-Ton Capacity Already Appears Sinocera disclosed this week that it has laid out both oxide and sulfide solid-state electrolytes, strategically focusing on the sulfide route. Its sulfide automated production line has been successfully completed, and product performance has been highly recognized by customers. This means domestic sulfide electrolyte capacity construction is transitioning from “pilot line” to “automated mass production line.” Shenzhen Xinyuanbang, in which Senior Technology holds a stake, already has thousand-ton oxide electrolyte capacity and hundred-ton shipments. Its “Guru” series achieved global mass production first in 2025, and it disclosed that global solid-state battery shipments will approach 750GWh in the next five years, with semi-solid-state accounting for over 80%, corresponding to an electrolyte membrane market of about 9.7 billion square meters. But capacity does not equal effective supply. SMM data show that China’s cumulative sulfide electrolyte output from January to August 2026 was less than 100 tons. Although up 119.7% year-on-year and already exceeding total 2025 output, the absolute volume remains very small. The pull of large-scale all-solid-state battery production on lithium sulfide cannot yet be verified from output data at this stage. 2.2 Cathode: Ultra-High-Nickel Exceeds 240mAh/g; Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Pricing System Starts Sichuan University released ultra-high-nickel all-solid-state battery results this week: ultra-high-nickel cathode material 0.1C discharge specific capacity exceeded 240mAh/g; solid-state battery energy density exceeded 400Wh/kg; cycle life reached over 800 cycles. This data is reference-significant in the cathode specific capacity dimension, but from lab indicators to mass production consistency, there is usually a 6–18 month engineering cycle. SMM added three lithium-rich manganese-based price points (high voltage 4.6–4.8V, medium voltage 4.45–4.55V, low voltage 4.25–4.4V), indicating that lithium-rich manganese-based materials, as one of the candidate solid-state battery cathode routes, have begun to form a quotable market prototype, but current trading activity is expected to be extremely low. 2.3 Anode: Silicon-Carbon Shipped in Batches; Dowstone Enters Cashing-In Period Dowstone confirmed this week that silicon-carbon anode has achieved batch shipments, and single-walled carbon nanotube-related products are supplied in batches to multiple cell manufacturers. This is the signal closest to “industrialization landing” on the material side this week—silicon-carbon anode’s leap from sample verification to batch shipment is substantially meaningful in the anode material field. But note: its solid electrolyte is only supplied in small batches to some customers, and the company is positioned as a “third tier” in the industry, with technical depth still lagging behind leading enterprises. artigo.texto: BIRMINGHAM, United Kingdom, Sept. 25, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Home energy brand SAMDUO has successfully concluded its showcase at Solar & Storage Live UK, drawing strong engagement from European installers, industry partners, distributors, and media seeking adaptable, space-conscious energy storage solutions. Throughout the event, SAMDUO presented its comprehensive line-up-featuring the modular Nex P2800 Pro for scalable capacity, the ultra-slim 11.9 cm Nex E6000 for shallow walls, and the compact Nex E6000H for more flexible placement in the home. Through live product demonstrations, guided stand tours, and App demonstrations, the Nex P2800 Pro showcased a modular approach to household energy storage, while the Nex E6000 and E6000H highlighted SAMDUO’s home-centred design approach for different residential spaces. Industry discussions at the stand highlighted several recurring topics, including space constraints, installation flexibility, and smart energy management. Conversations underscored growing interest in solutions defined not only by battery capacity, but by how naturally they fit into diverse living spaces, how easily they can be installed, and how effectively they integrate with solar generation and daily energy use. "European households don’t just need more storage capacity; they need systems that respect their physical living spaces and operate intelligently in the background,” said Kallen Lee, General Manager at SAMDUO. "The direct feedback from the exhibition validates our strategic direction-bringing true home energy intelligence to every home and empowering families to own their power as we build an integrated home-energy business across Europe.” At the exhibition, SAMDUO’s senior team also shared perspectives on European household-energy needs, market development, and the company’s longer-term direction in Europe-moving from individual storage products towards an integrated home-energy ecosystem combining hardware, software, and intelligent energy management. Looking ahead, SAMDUO will continue leveraging its two decades of experience in precision manufacturing, power, and energy storage to address key considerations around space, installation, safety, cost, and ecosystem compatibility across European residences. About SAMDUO SAMDUO develops intelligent home energy solutions for European households. Backed by two decades of experience in precision manufacturing, power and Energy Solutions, it combines engineering, product design and intelligent management around household space, installation, safety, cost and ecosystem compatibility. Home Energy Intelligence for every home. Own Your Power. Public transactions are sparse, and the reliability of price signals is limited. Core judgment: The core contradiction on the price side is not in the cathode or anode, but in lithium sulfide. The current battery-grade lithium sulfide price of RMB 1.3 million/t is still four times away from Gotion High-tech’s cost target of “lithium sulfide down to RMB 500,000/t and solid electrolyte down to RMB 300,000/t, entering the RMB 1/Wh era.” Several developments in this week’s documents—Sinocera’s sulfide electrolyte automated production line completed, Tengyuan Cobalt and Hunan Liuli jointly building a lithium sulfide pilot line—point precisely to attacking this bottleneck. II. Materials: Cathode, Anode, Electrolyte 2.1 Electrolyte: Sulfide Production Lines Completed in Clusters; Oxide Thousand-Ton Capacity Already Appears Sinocera disclosed this week that it has laid out both oxide and sulfide solid-state electrolytes, strategically focusing on the sulfide route. Its sulfide automated production line has been successfully completed, and product performance has been highly recognized by customers. This means domestic sulfide electrolyte capacity construction is transitioning from “pilot line” to “automated mass production line.” Shenzhen Xinyuanbang, in which Senior Technology holds a stake, already has thousand-ton oxide electrolyte capacity and hundred-ton shipments. Its “Guru” series achieved global mass production first in 2025, and it disclosed that global solid-state battery shipments will approach 750GWh in the next five years, with semi-solid-state accounting for over 80%, corresponding to an electrolyte membrane market of about 9.7 billion square meters. But capacity does not equal effective supply. SMM data show that China’s cumulative sulfide electrolyte output from January to August 2026 was less than 100 tons. Although up 119.7% year-on-year and already exceeding total 2025 output, the absolute volume remains very small. The pull of large-scale all-solid-state battery production on lithium sulfide cannot yet be verified from output data at this stage. 2.2 Cathode: Ultra-High-Nickel Exceeds 240mAh/g; Lithium-Rich Manganese-Based Pricing System Starts Sichuan University released ultra-high-nickel all-solid-state battery results this week: ultra-high-nickel cathode material 0.1C discharge specific capacity exceeded 240mAh/g; solid-state battery energy density exceeded 400Wh/kg; cycle life reached over 800 cycles. This data is reference-significant in the cathode specific capacity dimension, but from lab indicators to mass production consistency, there is usually a 6–18 month engineering cycle. SMM added three lithium-rich manganese-based price points (high voltage 4.6–4.8V, medium voltage 4.45–4.55V, low voltage 4.25–4.4V), indicating that lithium-rich manganese-based materials, as one of the candidate solid-state battery cathode routes, have begun to form a quotable market prototype, but current trading activity is expected to be extremely low. 2.3 Anode: Silicon-Carbon Shipped in Batches; Dowstone Enters Cashing-In Period Dowstone confirmed this week that silicon-carbon anode has achieved batch shipments, and single-walled carbon nanotube-related products are supplied in batches to multiple cell manufacturers. This is the signal closest to “industrialization landing” on the material side this week—silicon-carbon anode’s leap from sample verification to batch shipment is substantially meaningful in the anode material field. But note: its solid electrolyte is only supplied in small batches to some customers, and the company is positioned as a “third tier” in the industry, with technical depth still lagging behind leading enterprises. artigo.texto: LA VERNE, Calif. (KABC) -- A fire erupted at a battery storage unit at a Metropolitan Water District facility in La Verne on Tuesday, prompting nearby schools to evacuate. The lithium battery fire was reported around 11:40 a.m. near a solar panel field on the northeast side of the facility in the 3200 block of Wheeler Avenue. Crews from the La Verne Fire Department and Los Angeles County Fire Department responded. One employee suffered minor injuries and was taken to a local hospital, according to La Verne Fire Department Battalion Chief Mark Savage. Shortly after 3 p.m., the L.A. County Fire Department said the fire had been knocked down. AIR7 video shows firefighters dousing the flames with water. La Verne fire crews were still monitoring the scene and mopping up, noting that there was still a risk, with more lithium batteries at the site. By Tuesday evening, no flare-ups had been reported, and crews were using a drone to monitor the batteries. Firefighters estimate there are fewer than 20 lithium batteries in the storage facility. "These things do not like any kind of additional heat, and the understanding is, there is something going on with that bank now that it is reacting to the previous heat that it was exposed to," said Batt. Chief Mark Savage. "So we are monitoring closely. We have reinitiated cooling measures for that battery bank now. But it's one of those things that, once it gets started, it's extremely difficult to stop, if not impossible to stop." The fire prompted evacuation orders and warnings near Bonita Avenue and Wheeler Avenue and a shelter-in-place for the surrounding residential neighborhood. Click here to see if you are in an impacted area. Some evacuation orders were later downgraded to warnings. By early Tuesday evening, firefighters said the orders were only impacting the approximately 185 properties closest to the facility. La Verne police said shopping centers along Wheeler Avenue north of Foothill Boulevard were evacuated as a precaution. Grace Miller Elementary School, located just east of the facility, was under a shelter-in-place order, and Holly Oak Street south of the campus was closed to traffic. Savage said students appeared to be released from the school while firefighters battled the blaze. Parents told Eyewitness News that Ramona Middle School and Bonita High School were also affected. Holy Name of Mary School, Damien High School and the University of La Verne were evacuated. The university said all classes were canceled until further notice. Eyewitness News spoke to Ramona Middle School parents who arrived to pick up their kids. By the time most parents arrived, it was already the school's normal pick-up time. "They're blocking off Wheeler, so it makes it a little hectic but scary at the same time, so we're just here getting the kids out of safety," said parent Irene Flores. "We got it on our phones, the emergency message to evacuate our facility. So might as well come get the kids, make sure they're safe," said parent Jason Wagner. "In La Verne, we've never seen these kind of things." The Metropolitan Water District said its water supply was not affected by the fire. The cause of the fire is still under investigation. Savage said nothing like this has happened there before, but it's raising concerns for neighbors who had no clue that the water treatment plant housed massive battery banks with the potential to catch fire. If you're wondering if you live near a facility that houses potentially dangerous or hazardous items, you can find out. Back in May, 7 On Your Side did an investigation and we shared the Environmental Protection Agency's interactive map, where you can learn about the enforcement and compliance history of facilities near you. City News Service contributed to this report.

artigo.texto: What are consumers who fixate on battery performance when shopping for cars afraid of? If we take 2021 as the inflection point for the accelerated sales growth of new energy vehicles in China, this round of popularization has gone through five years by this year. As the driving range and service time continue to accumulate, some problems that were not obvious in the early stage have gradually emerged, among which the power battery has attracted the most attention. Last year, a Chinese self-owned brand filed a lawsuit against a second-tier power battery supplier over cell quality and related losses; earlier this year, a luxury brand launched a global recall for some vehicles due to the risk of overheating in partial battery modules that may cause fires; a few months later, the "banana battery" incident once again sparked huge public controversy. Apart from safety incidents, battery issues are also increasingly frequently included in daily vehicle complaint cases. The Q2 2026 report released by CarQuality.cn shows that "power battery failure" entered the TOP 20 new energy vehicle complaint problems for the first time, ranking 6th, with the number of fault complaints doubling month-on-month; in the same period, the complaint volume of pure electric vehicles increased by 70.2% month-on-month. Regulatory standards are also tightening accordingly. The mandatory national standard GB 38031—2025 *Safety Requirements for Traction Batteries Used in Electric Vehicles* issued by the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology has been implemented since July 1, 2026, further strengthening safety requirements such as "no fire, no explosion". Authorities including the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology have previously required vehicle manufacturers and power battery enterprises to jointly investigate abnormalities in temperature, voltage, current, insulation and other indicators, and form a closed loop of risk warning, fault handling and after-sales service. Most consumers are unable to study every parameter and test item of batteries one by one; after an accident, it is also difficult for them to identify which link the responsibility lies in on their own. For ordinary people, one of the most intuitive solutions is to find a trustworthy battery brand, and then include models equipped with that brand's batteries in their selection range. A large number of consumers have chosen CATL to take on this role. According to NielsenIQ's 2026 Global New Energy Vehicle Consumer Research Report, 37.1% of Chinese respondents said they would consider giving up purchasing their desired model if it is not equipped with CATL batteries. The era has come when a single battery can determine whether a vehicle is purchased or not. 01 Why do consumers choose vehicles based on battery brands? In the era of fuel vehicles, few people would ask who supplies the fuel tank or a core component of the engine before buying a car. In the era of new energy vehicles, however, batteries can hardly stay hidden behind the vehicle brand, as they determine safety, driving range, energy replenishment efficiency, vehicle residual value and long-term maintenance cost at the same time. In the NielsenIQ survey, 80% of Chinese respondents believe that battery is the key factor determining the safety of new energy vehicles, and another 80% think that battery quality represents the overall quality of the vehicle. The gap between the actual driving range and the nominal driving range is the most prominent pain point in current battery experience; the charging speed presents a mismatch of "high importance, low satisfaction". For car owners, these problems will finally converge into a simple judgment: after several years, the battery determines whether the car can still complete daily travel safely and stably. The difficulty lies in that a power battery never works independently as a single cell. Cells, modules, Pack structure, thermal management system, software warning and vehicle layout together form the safety chain. Any deviation in any link may be manifested as a "battery problem". The recall of a new vehicle-making force brand is a direct example: the risk source points to the anti-corrosion performance of coolant, while the final disposal covers coolant, power battery and front motor controller. Commercial disputes can also reflect the complexity of responsibility boundaries. Last year, a Chinese self-owned brand filed a lawsuit against a second-tier power battery supplier over cell quality and related losses. It also takes a long process for carmakers and suppliers to clarify the responsibilities among cells, system integration, verification standards and actual use scenarios. Similar problems did not appear for the first time. In 2019, multiple fire accidents occurred after a model under the new energy brand of a traditional carmaker was launched. A senior executive of the carmaker's battery business summarized the responsibility attribution dilemma in the industry at that time very directly: vehicle manufacturers may look for causes from the battery, while battery enterprises will also check the vehicle system design; some accidents cannot be fully reproduced in the laboratory, and the legal proof and compensation boundaries are very complicated. When the responsibility division is inherently difficult, the subsequent handling can hardly fully meet the expectations of car owners. Therefore, brands begin to play the role of "risk compressor". The NielsenIQ survey shows that 79% of respondents believe there are obvious quality differences between different battery brands, 79% think that well-known and high-quality battery brands will increase their willingness to buy cars, and 76% are willing to pay extra fees for that. artigo.texto: KOTA KINABALU (Sept 24): Sabah state government will not allow unvetted carbon market projects to be rushed to market or traded on speculation despite the immense opportunities in the sector. Chief Minister Datuk Seri Hajiji Noor stressed that the state government will protect Sabah’s reputation and brand through strong regulatory discipline. He said poorly designed projects, overstated climate claims, undervalued resources and the exclusion of native communities will undermine investor confidence in Sabah's carbon credits. “It is therefore in Sabah’s commercial interest to uphold the highest standards of environmental, social, financial, and governance integrity. Buyers will demand full transparency,” he said at the Sabah Carbon Market Forum: Unlocking Carbon Market Opportunities here Thursday. Sabah Deputy Chief Minister II cum State Finance Minister Datuk Seri Masidi Manjun delivered his speech. Hajiji said laws like the Sabah Climate Change and Carbon Governance Enactment 2025 legally recognise the state government’s ownership of carbon rights and set clear rules for carbon-related activities, including project approval and credit trading. “The Sabah Climate Change Action Council (SCCAC) will oversee the state’s climate policy, prepare the state carbon budget for ministerial approval and gazettement, and coordinate efforts between state and federal agencies. “The Sabah Climate Registry and Inventory Centre will provide technical and operational support to the SCCAC. Together, this framework is intended to offer investors a transparent, coordinated regulatory gateway for project approvals and registration of carbon rights,” he said. He added that Sabah has Malaysia's first nature-based verified carbon credit initiative through the Kuamut Rainforest Conservation Project, which spans some 83,381 hectares (ha) of the state’s rich lowland and hill forests. The project, expected to reduce carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions by about 800,000 tonnes, has set the benchmark for future initiatives. BeZero Carbon, the global carbon credit ratings agency, rated the project best-in-class. The chief minister said the state government is also developing a diversified portfolio of carbon assets across key economic sectors, including the blue economy, agriculture, renewable energy and green technology, as well as carbon capture and storage. Under the blue economy sector, Hajiji said Sabah has the largest continuous mangrove area of more than 340,000 ha in Malaysia. Sabah has strong potential to become a regional leader in the sector through marine biotechnology, sustainable aquaculture, and marine ecosystem-based tourism. In agriculture, Sabah’s oil palm industry covers nearly 1.5 million ha, offering significant opportunities for methane capture and other climate mitigation initiatives using agricultural waste. For the renewable energy and green technology sector, the state government will continue expanding solar, hydropower, biomass, and biogas to provide reliable, accessible, and affordable energy guided by the Sabah Energy Roadmap and Master Plan 2040. “Sabah aims to increase the share of renewable electricity by 2030 through solar, hydropower, and biomass projects,” he said. In the carbon capture and storage sector, Hajiji said Sabah’s offshore geological basins, together with its maritime frontier, offer long-term potential for geological carbon storage and position Sabah as a nationally significant industrial storage hub serving the region. Almost 30% of Sabah’s landmass is designated totally protected areas, contributing to Malaysia’s biodiversity commitments and the 2030 global conservation target under the Kunming-Montreal Global Biodiversity Framework. This places the state prominently on the global conservation map, he said. “Sabah is also Malaysia’s primary net carbon sink, or carbon-negative state, based on greenhouse gas inventory data. Our extensive forest cover strengthens Malaysia’s overall carbon absorption capacity of roughly 36%. “Through inclusive forest management, created in partnership with local communities, we strive to balance environmental conservation with the socio-economic wellbeing of our people. Sabah’s identity and future are deeply rooted in our natural heritage,” he said. Uploaded by Magessan Varatharaja

artigo.texto: Data centers drawing 25 megawatts or more of electricity are no longer allowed on Allegheny County-owned property. County Council voted unanimously Tuesday to prohibit the construction, operation or establishment of large-scale data centers — and the infrastructure built specifically to support them — on county-owned land and in county-owned buildings. The measure does not restrict data centers on privately owned property, leaving those land-use decisions to individual municipalities. The ordinance had broad support ahead of Tuesday’s votes, with council’s Sustainability and Green Initiatives Committee unanimously advancing it last week. Sponsors of the bill include President Michelle Naccarati-Chapkis, D-Plum; Dan Grzybek, D-Bethel Park; Kathleen Madonna-Emmerling, D-Moon; Lissa Geiger Shulman, D-Hampton; Pat Catena, D-Carnegie; Paul Klein, D-Pittsburgh; Jordan Botta, D-Bloomfield; and at-large members Bethany Hallam, D-North Side, and Alex Rose, I-Squirrel Hill. On Tuesday, Rose, who chairs the Sustainability and Green Initiatives Committee, explained to the council that the committee adopted an amendment to help avoid accidentally banning servers from “existing on Allegheny property” and avoid unintended impacts on facilities such as county server operations and the 911 center. Under the bill, infrastructure associated with data centers, including generators, utility lines, cooling water and wastewater treatment facilities, water-holding facilities, pump stations, water towers and other environmental controls are prohibited. Also, county property can no longer be used for data center ancillary use or secondary structures such as administrative, logistical, fiber optic, storage and security buildings or structures. The council opted not to impose a countywide land-use ban because, under Pennsylvania law, zoning and land-use decisions involving private property are made by individual municipalities rather than the county. Private developers could still potentially propose a data center in a municipality subject to that municipality’s zoning and other applicable laws. Some municipalities in Allegheny County already host existing smaller data centers or have larger projects proposed. In Springdale, a major planned data center would stand 75 feet tall and stretch over 652,000 square feet. Several boroughs and townships, including East Deer, Oakmont, Tarentum, Upper Burrell, Murrysville and Gilpin, have adopted or are in the process of implementing ordinances similar to the county in an effort to regulate data center development.

artigo.texto: DEBRECEN, Hungary, Sept. 22, 2026 /PRNewswire/ -- CATL begins trial production on 22 September 2026 in its newly built cell factory in Debrecen as the company had fulfilled all preconditions required to commence trial run. The purpose of trial production is to set up, optimise and validate the production equipment and manufacturing processes ahead of the start of series production. CATL Debrecen continues cooperating and working closely with the government and the authorities in order to keep high standards on the environmental issues as well as the health and safety of its employees. CATL announced the construction of its second European battery plant in Debrecen in August 2022, with the aim of integrating to the European automotive and e-mobility supply chain and better serve leading European automakers. Construction of the first cell building started in summer 2023 and by spring 2026 the building had been equipped with the most advanced technology. After obtaining the occupancy permit in August 2026, the company obtained all relevant permits and completed all pre-conditions required by its IPPC permit prior to start trial operations from 22 September on the first two production lines of its cell manufacturing facility. Prior to issuing the occupancy permit, the Hajdú-Bihar County Government Office carried out regular on-site inspections at CATL's facilities in order to follow up on previous issues creating serious worries in local inhabitants. Authority representatives confirmed that the company had resolved all deficiencies identified earlier in the permitting process. As a strategic manufacturing hub, CATL's Debrecen plant will supply the most well-known, leading European automakers, which have already built significant electric vehicle production capacity in Hungary in recent years. As a global technology leader CATL implemented the most advanced, flexible production lines in Debrecen in order to fulfil the needs of its valued clients at all times. The company has already been manufacturing battery modules since autumn 2024 in Debrecen and has already produced 537,000 modules ever since. Once all facilities ready, the Hungarian plant will be CATL's largest manufacturing base outside China with a 100 GWH capacity. Alongside obtaining the permits and completing pre-conditions required to launch trial operations, CATL Debrecen remains committed to working closely with the Government and the authorities to prioritize the health and safety of its employees. Furthermore, employee health, safety and environmental factors will be thoroughly monitored during the trial operation as well, and results will be submitted to the Authority proactively. CATL's investment is not only important for Debrecen and its region, but also for the Hungarian economy and the European e-mobility supply chain. CATL is committed to transparency and welcomes the authorities to visit its site at any time. PR Newswire Asia Ltd. artigo.texto: OLYMPIA — Washington Governor Bob Ferguson and California Governor Gavin Newsom announced they have taken the next steps toward Washington joining the California–Québec carbon market in 2027. Together, these three jurisdictions would rank as the third-largest economy in the world. Washington crossed a major milestone. The state concluded its linkage process by finalizing regulatory changes that make Washington’s market compatible with the California–Québec carbon market, such as aligning rules for how auctions are conducted. With that, Washington completed the steps it needs to take in order to link markets, the culmination of three years of rigorous analysis and public engagement. Governor Newsom shared today that he has authorized California to move forward with linkage, making the formal findings legally required for California to move ahead with the final step to link the two markets. California law requires that the Governor make specific findings about a partner state’s carbon market before the California Air Resources Board (CARB) may proceed with linking markets. California’s action allows CARB to begin the public regulatory process in that state — the final step before the markets are formally linked. Québec is also working toward regulatory updates this year. Earlier this year, the three jurisdictions signed a linkage agreement that laid the groundwork for joint operations. The jurisdictions are expected to link markets in 2027. “States and subnational governments are stepping up and leading at a time when the federal government is trying to dismantle U.S. climate policy,” said Governor Ferguson. “Linkage isn’t just good climate policy — it’s smart economics. Linking will unlock greater emissions reductions, lower the cost of clean technologies, and create good‑paying jobs in high‑growth industries. We’re excited to be moving forward.” “California has long shown climate action means a stronger economy, cleaner air, and billions of dollars of investment back into communities across our state,” Governor Newsom said. “Meanwhile, Donald Trump and his big-polluter cronies are hell-bent on doing the opposite: more pollution, more uncertainty, and higher costs for working families. California is choosing a different path. We’re choosing certainty, partnership, and clean energy. By joining forces with our partner in Washington state, we will build a stronger, more durable carbon market that will drive investment, cut pollution, and power the clean economy of the future.” California was the first U.S. state to launch a carbon market in 2013. In 2014, it joined with the Canadian province of Québec. In 2023, Washington became the second U.S. state to launch a carbon market. Washington’s market was designed to link so businesses could access the benefits of a larger market. This unprecedented climate partnership means businesses in all three jurisdictions can make more predictable, long-term investments in reducing greenhouse gases. With greater investment, the cost of emission-reducing technologies will go down, leading to even higher rates of adoption and local economic benefits like job growth. Putting an economy‑wide price on greenhouse gas emissions is widely seen as the best policy tool for addressing climate change, and carbon markets are the most affordable way to do it. In this market-based system, the state sets an overall limit on emissions that declines each year, but it does not set the price of emissions. Instead, the price is set through auctions where companies compete to purchase allowances for every metric ton of greenhouse gases they emit. The price can easily adapt to changes in market conditions, and companies that can reduce emissions at the lowest cost move first. In a linked market, each jurisdiction will contribute their supply of allowances to joint auctions, creating a single carbon price across all three. Larger markets provide more stable prices, and price stability is a key part of accelerating decarbonization because it gives businesses the certainty they need to plan for long‑term, capital‑intensive projects. Over time, as more companies invest in emissions‑reducing technologies, those technologies become cheaper, making it easier for others to take action. The Washington-California-Québec carbon market is expected to lead to greater total emissions reductions across the three jurisdictions. Washington’s addition to the market also creates momentum for other states and other subnational governments to implement linkage‑ready carbon markets by paving a clear pathway for others to follow.

artigo.texto: Just one year ago, 33% of Americans regularly used AI. Today, that figure is nearing 50% and continues to rise rapidly. The models are changing rapidly, and while US providers currently dominate the market, emerging providers from Asia and Europe are entering the space, making the AI landscape agile and diverse. Users must therefore consider which model best fits their specific requirements. For engineers, the main question is entirely different. Regardless of the model or algorithm, every AI request demands enormous computing power. Behind every AI model are thousands of processors across hundreds of server racks housed in data centers. Image Credit: KM Stock/Shutterstock.com Engineers must supply consistent, reliable power to the racks while removing heat from key infrastructure. Data center engineers must consider the following questions: - How can power supply and distribution be optimized? - How can cooling and thermal management be enhanced? - How can reliability be ensured? - How can systems be protected against fire and thermal runaway? - How does all this scale? Seemingly minor components play a crucial role in data center design and function. This article explores how innovative material solutions can support safer, more reliable, and future-ready data centers. Enhance Power Distribution in Data Centers with Tapes Data centers are complex systems with thousands of microprocessors at their hearts, beating with an extremely high electric pulse. To keep this pulse running, they need electric energy. So much energy, in fact that supplying and managing it on-site is a critical consideration with no room for failure. For this reason, many data centers are fitted with on-site power generation and large battery energy storage systems (BESS) to ensure they remain operational during energy shortages or fluctuations. Within these BESS, innovative foams such as the Norseal® TRP Series offer high protection against thermal runaway events and can help prolong battery service life, while Norgard® Tapes provide electrical insulation and protection against elevated temperatures. Power distribution in data centers extends beyond BESS and power generation. A primary objective is distributing power to servers and microprocessors. To ensure low-loss, safe power distribution, specialty tapes optimize electrical insulation, busbar isolation, wire and cable protection, and EMI shielding for safe, dependable operation. Beyond enhancing safety, advanced insulation and protection materials help preserve electrical integrity in challenging operating environments. This improves system dependability and extends service life for critical power infrastructure. For data center operators, these advantages translate directly into increased uptime and reduced total cost of ownership. How Innovative Tapes Can Enhance Thermal Management Substantial computing power, processor performance, and server density come with a drawback: every watt a processor consumes eventually becomes heat that must be removed effectively to maintain performance, reliability, and operational safety. Consequently, thermal management has become one of the most crucial engineering challenges in contemporary data centers. For engineers, maintaining servers and processors at controlled temperatures is essential for server performance, longevity, and safety. Advanced materials can prevent unwanted heat transfer through thermal insulation or facilitate heat dissipation through thermally conductive interfaces. By managing thermal energy where it is generated, these materials contribute to stable operating conditions and help safeguard delicate electronic components. With extensive experience in EV batteries, Saint-Gobain’s Thermal Gap Fillers, tapes, and coated fabrics have verified performance under demanding conditions. The company’s specially formulated materials deliver exceptional dielectric strength, thermal stability, and long-term reliability under harsh conditions. While these materials help create ideal operating conditions, their key advantages matter most when excess heat could reach levels that affect other components. The Foams That Support Reliable Cooling Modern high-density computing environments have pushed standard air-cooling technologies past their capabilities. Advanced liquid-cooling systems are currently being implemented to eliminate excess heat from servers, processors, and the chips themselves. Whether the topic is Direct-to-Chip, Door Heat Exchangers, or full Immersion Cooling, sealing is a crucial engineering consideration. Even minor leaks can decrease cooling efficiency, raise energy consumption, and damage sensitive equipment. Meticulously engineered seals and gaskets enhance performance while protecting against temperature variations, vibration, and challenging cooling media to deliver low-maintenance dependability for long-term service. Solutions such as Norseal AGP200 offer exceptional conformability, outstanding sealing and gasketing characteristics, and excellent durability. They are also manufactured with bio-based materials to improve indoor air quality, reduce VOCs, and lower the environmental footprint. While most PUR foams utilize oil-based ingredients, Norseal AGP200 utilizes predominantly bio-based polyols without compromising performance. AGP200 requires just 30% compression to provide a water seal and thermal insulation. It offers exceptional conformability and low compression force, enabling cost savings through material reduction. By preventing air and liquid leakage, improving thermal insulation, and supporting long-term system dependability, advanced foam solutions help data center operators optimize cooling efficiency, reduce maintenance needs, and maintain uninterrupted operation of critical AI infrastructure. artigo.texto: Supercapacitors are well positioned to see deployment in data centers, in order to solve the challenge of protecting data center equipment from rapid power demand surges and voltage drops caused by AI training and prompting. In total, the market for supercapacitors in data centers is expected to reach over US$950 million by 2037 according to IDTechEx's recent report "Supercapacitors for Data Centers 2027-2037: Technologies, Applications, Players and Forecasts." However, several questions remain for supercapacitor deployers and data center operators: where and how exactly should supercapacitors be effectively deployed? AI Data Usage Patterns - Voltage Sags, Peak Shaving and Critical Load Requirements Hyperscale data centers are seeing significant construction, driven primarily by deployment of AI across a number of industries and services. AI data centers have distinct power demand profiles compared to conventional data centers, due to large transient loads and short-term peaks in power demand. These spikes can be challenging for conventional power architecture to handle. Extreme power demand spikes lead to voltage sags, which in turn can lead to temporary shutting down of servers, equipment failures and grid-wide instability. Solving these issues can help to make AI data centers both more profitable and more palatable for neighboring authorities and locations that might otherwise oppose development. Power architecture and backup power systems must therefore be adapted to handle AI power profiles. This requires rapid charging/discharging times (as spikes can be at ms-scale), durability over many charge-discharge cycles, high power density (to reduce footprint for large critical loads) and easy integration into existing power architectures (especially for retrofitting of data centers). Supercapacitors are well positioned for this use-case, as is explored in IDTechEx's recent report. Data Center Architecture Data center designs vary depending on the data center type, location and power supply. However, several features of data center power architectures are consistent. Computations are performed by servers within a rack, which also contains switches, routers, storage and rack-level backup power, e.g. battery backup units (BBUs). Multiple racks are placed together to form an aisle, at the end of which is the power distribution unit (PDU), which routes power to the racks from the facility's centralized power room and includes buffering devices to protect equipment from power surges. The facility's centralized power room will contain both power architecture connecting the facility to the grid, or routing electricity from the grid connection point to the aisles, as well as uninterruptible power supply (UPS), in the form of battery storage units, which will be turned on automatically in the event of a blackout, to bridge the gap between grid outage and diesel generator activation. Supercapacitors may be deployed at rack-, aisle- and UPS room-level, offering different advantages and disadvantages depending on placement. Supercapacitor Placement: In-Rack, In-Aisle or In UPS Facility In-rack supercapacitor placements, e.g. within BBUs, are likely to be optimal for new-build AI data centers. This is because in-rack deployment allows for voltage stabilization of low-voltage equipment within the rack/server, which might not otherwise be sufficiently protected from power demand surges at the rack-level. In addition, by deploying at the rack-level, supercapacitor deployments can be made more specific, thereby potentially reducing the overall power demand. For example, in a data center in which not all racks will be utilized for AI, or in which training/prompting is split from standard computation, supercapacitor deployments at rack-level may be limited to appropriate racks. However, aisle-level and UPS room-level deployments are likely to be easier in terms of retrofitting, as well as allowing for higher compute density within the rack. IDTechEx predicts that this will lead to aisle-level and UPS room-level deployments being more popular in the short term, especially in co-location data centers. UPS room-level deployments offer an additional advantage compared to rack-level deployments, in that a rack-level deployment will not protect high-voltage equipment and power architecture at the facility level, for example cooling systems. As a result, IDTechEx predicts that by 2037, rack-level and UPS room-level deployments will be the most popular for supercapacitors in data centers. For a more detailed analysis of supercapacitor placement, as well as application and use-case analysis, see the recent report by IDTechEx: "Supercapacitors for Data Centers 2027-2037: Technologies, Applications, Players and Forecasts".

artigo.texto: According to EnergyTrend, Growatt issued a product price adjustment notice to its dealer partners on September 21. The company plans to raise prices of inverters and energy storage systems by 510%, effective October 8. In the notice, Growatt stated that rising upstream rawmaterial costs and tight supply of core components have lifted overall production costs. While the firm has absorbed cost pressures via supplychain optimization and internal costreduction measures, cost increases have exceeded its tolerance threshold, prompting price adjustments for selected products. Per the document, two major product categories are subject to the price hike: - String inverters, including gridtied inverters and storage inverters: 510% price increase; - Energy storage systems, including commercial & industrial energystorage cabinets and residential energystorage systems: 510% price increase. The notice specifies October 8 as the effective date. Orders with completed contracts and payments prior to the effective date will remain at the original prices. Based on incomplete statistics from EnergyTrend, more than ten energystoragerelated enterprises including Sungrow, EVE Energy and East have released pricerevision notices since July this year. Adjusted products cover lithiumion batteries, power conversion systems (PCS), solarstoragecharging integrated equipment and residential energystorage products, with price hikes ranging from 2% to as high as 30%. Source：EnergyTrend

artigo.texto: Global Activated Carbon Market Outlook 2026-2033: Water Treatment, Air Purification and Emissions Control Demand Surges Stricter air and water rules and rising purification needs are driving demand, creating opportunities in Asia-Pacific, specialty filtration and sustainable activated carbon Dublin, Sept. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- "Activated Carbon Market Insights, Competitive Landscape, and Market Forecast - 2033" has been added to ResearchAndMarkets.com's offering. The global activated carbon market is projected to expand from USD 6.1 billion in 2026 to USD 11.1 billion by 2033, registering a compound annual growth rate of 8.90% during the forecast period. Market growth is being supported by stricter environmental regulations, increased investment in water treatment infrastructure, heightened awareness of air quality, and expanding industrial and consumer applications. Activated Carbon Market Overview Demand for activated carbon continues to rise across water treatment, air and gas purification, food and beverage processing, pharmaceuticals, chemicals, electronics, and environmental remediation. Rapid industrialization and urbanization, particularly in emerging economies, are increasing the need for effective purification, filtration, decolorization, and odor-control technologies. Advancements in powdered and granular activated carbon production are also improving performance, adsorption capacity, and cost efficiency. Innovation in steam and chemical activation processes is enabling manufacturers to develop specialized products for municipal, industrial, healthcare, and household applications. Key Market Growth Drivers - Environmental regulations: Governments are implementing increasingly stringent standards governing industrial emissions, wastewater discharge, drinking water quality, and volatile organic compounds. These measures are accelerating the adoption of activated carbon in environmental compliance systems. - Water treatment demand: Population growth, urban development, industrial activity, and concerns about water contamination are driving investment in municipal and industrial water treatment. Activated carbon is widely used to reduce organic compounds, chemicals, odors, and other contaminants. - Industrial and consumer applications: Food and beverage producers, pharmaceutical companies, chemical manufacturers, and electronics businesses are increasing their use of activated carbon. Consumer demand for household water filters and indoor air purification systems is also contributing to market expansion. - Technology development: Improvements in activation processes and application-specific product design are supporting higher efficiency and broader commercial adoption. Emerging Business Opportunities The activated carbon market presents significant opportunities for manufacturers, technology providers, and filtration specialists. Asia-Pacific offers particularly strong potential due to rapid industrial development, expanding urban populations, and growing investment in water and air purification infrastructure. Customized activated carbon products for industrial emission controls, respiratory protection, specialty filtration, healthcare, food safety, and gas purification represent promising areas for innovation. Demand for sustainable products and responsible raw material sourcing is also creating opportunities for companies to strengthen differentiation and respond to corporate environmental goals. Regional Market Analysis - North America: Market growth is supported by established water treatment systems, industrial emission requirements, environmental investment, and the presence of major activated carbon suppliers. - Europe: Strong environmental protection policies and sustained demand from pharmaceutical, chemical, food processing, and municipal water treatment applications continue to support adoption. - Asia-Pacific: The region is expected to lead global market growth through 2033. China and India are experiencing rising demand across municipal water treatment, industrial purification, manufacturing, and emission-control applications. - Latin America: Investment in water infrastructure and increasing awareness of environmental sustainability are creating new opportunities across the region. - Middle East and Africa: Water scarcity, industrial development, and the need for efficient purification systems are supporting steady market expansion. Competitive Landscape The global activated carbon market remains competitive, with companies pursuing capacity expansions, strategic partnerships, acquisitions, and product development initiatives. Notable market participants include Calgon Carbon Corporation, Jacobi Carbons AB, Kuraray Co., Ltd., Haycarb PLC, Donau Carbon GmbH, Oxbow Activated Carbon LLC, Carbotech AC GmbH & Co. KG, Ingevity Corporation, Norit, and other regional manufacturers. Competition is expected to intensify as suppliers invest in higher-performance products, sustainable production methods, localized manufacturing, and application-specific solutions. Companies capable of maintaining reliable supply chains while meeting evolving environmental and quality standards are likely to secure a stronger market position. artigo.texto: Pulaski County's first data center ordinance awaits judge's signature; no AVAIO carve-out LITTLE ROCK, Ark. (KATV) — The Pulaski County Quorum Court on Tuesday passed the county's first ordinance regulating data centers in an 11 to 4 vote. County Judge Barry Hyde has five days left to approve or veto that legislation, the fruit of nearly half a year of tense debate and input from concerned members of the public. The ordinance classifies large data centers as heavy industrial land uses requiring conditional use permits. And, the ordinance did not grandfather in the company AVAIO Digital's planned $6 billion data center near Wrightsville. AVAIO Digital is in the midst of a permitting process that recognizes its data center as a warehouse or office space rather than heavy industry. The planned facility's campus will encompass 760 acres and, fully built out as an estimated $21 billion investment, may pull over a gigawatt from the power grid and be one of the largest data centers in the country. Pulaski County's new ordinance would suddenly impose sweeping requirements for AVAIO, which it does not provide a carve-out for. "I did not think it was fair to let one company opt out on the rules just because they were first," Pulaski County Justice of the Peace Julie Blackwood, the lead sponsor of the data center ordinance, said. The Quorum Court passed the ordinance prepared for the possibility of a lawsuit. "If it does pass, if it does get in, then we were going to have to go into them proving vested rights, how much they've got...what all falls under our ordinance and what they can claim does not. And those will be legal battles probably fought out with attorneys," Blackwood said. So what does the ordinance do? First off, it creates an intensive application and conditional use permit process giving the county detailed information on proposed data centers before they're approved and requiring applicants to show the facilities won't place an undue burden on the local grid, water supply, or other infrastructure. The ordinance sets noise limits and requires a 500-foot setback from residential properties. It allows the county to place project-specific limits on power and water use, noise, and other impacts. It also requires additional review when a data center expands and requires data center operators to maintain a plan and provide financial assurance for eventual decommissioning. Those are just the bullet points from a comprehensive ordinance that resulted from months of tense debate, wide public interest and input, and a lot of learning about the fast emerging data center industry. "You know, I think that was one of the reasons it was so difficult to get it all passed, just because it is it is difficult legislation to understand...it's brand new for everybody," Blackwood said. But now it's all up to County Judge Barry Hyde, who has the power to veto the ordinance but is facing significant public pressure to approve it. "I think the public wants him to sign it...And this is something I think is very important is that we need to listen to our constituents. So hopefully he will sign it and won't veto it," Blackwood told KATV.

artigo.texto: Gigante chinesa de tecnologia anuncia expansão de seus centros de dados na Europa e no Oriente Médio Anúncio ocorre pouco antes de reunião entre Xi Jinping e Donald Trump, que será realizada em Washington, onde se espera que ambos líderes discutam questões comerciais Gigante chinesa de tecnologia, Alibaba anuncia expansão de seus centros de dados no exterior — Foto: Wang Zhao/AFP A gigante de tecnológica chinesa Alibaba anunciou, nesta quarta-feira, um plano para expandir seus centros de dados no exterior, com o objetivo de alcançar mercados em toda a Europa e no Oriente Médio. O Alibaba, sediado em Hangzhou, é um dos líderes do comércio eletrônico e da indústria de inteligência artificial da China. Seu modelo Qwen está entre os mais baixados do mundo. A empresa informou que "estabelecerá suas primeiras zonas de nuvem" na Turquia, na Finlândia e nos Países Baixos, ao mesmo tempo em que "ampliará sua presença de centros de dados na Malásia, na Alemanha, nos Emirados Árabes Unidos, na França e em Hong Kong" nos próximos 12 meses. O anúncio ocorreu antes da aguardada reunião entre o presidente chinês, Xi Jinping, e seu homólogo americano, Donald Trump, em Washington, onde se espera que ambos os líderes discutam questões comerciais, entre outros temas. As duas potências estão envolvidas em uma rivalidade tecnológica que se concentra cada vez mais em indústrias de vanguarda, como semicondutores, IA e robótica. O Alibaba tem como meta alcançar mais de 20 gigawatts de capacidade global em centros de dados até 2032, disse Wu durante a conferência anual mais importante da empresa em Hangzhou. A companhia também apresentou no evento um novo chip de IA, o Zhenwu V900, afirmando que ele oferecerá o triplo do desempenho de seu antecessor. artigo.texto: SAN DIEGO – September 23, 2026 – Procopio helped secure unanimous approval from the San Diego County Board of Supervisors for Starlight Solar, a major solar and battery energy storage project planned for Boulevard in eastern San Diego County. Starlight Solar will help advance regional and state renewable energy goals. Environmental organizations and labor representatives spoke in support of the project before the Board of Supervisors, and the project developer entered into a labor agreement providing for the use of local union workers during construction. The 588-acre project will include a solar facility capable of generating up to 100 megawatts and a 217-megawatt battery energy storage system developed in two phases. First proposed in 2022, Starlight Solar also received unanimous approval from the San Diego County Planning Commission before advancing to the Board of Supervisors. Procopio represented the project developer throughout the entitlement process, led by Partner and Land Use Practice Leader Jim Vaughn and Associate Matt Abbot. The project team worked closely with James Whalen, President of J. Whalen Associates, Inc., who served as land use consultant for the project and led the entitlement and public outreach efforts. The Environmental Impact Report was prepared by SWCA Environmental Consultants. “This approval reflects years of work by a large team that took the community’s concerns seriously while working through an unusually complex entitlement process,” said Vaughn. “We addressed evolving questions surrounding battery storage and fire safety, worked through environmental and land use issues, and overcame a CEQA challenge ambush delivered the day before the final hearing. Securing unanimous support from both the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors is a significant victory for a project of this scale and complexity.” The project also includes a community benefits package intended to support local community-determined uses, as well as funding for renovation of Boulevard’s community center. The project will be built on land that has been in the Haagen family for more than sixty years, and family members have made numerous contributions to the community over the decades. Phase I is expected to break ground in approximately a year. “This was a true team effort, with many people playing important roles in an unprecedented approval process,” said Whalen. “The project earned unanimous decisions from both the Planning Commission and Board of Supervisors while breaking new ground in areas including battery safety analysis and community benefits. It shows what can be accomplished when a project team engages seriously with regulators, environmental organizations and the community.” About Procopio Procopio represents developers, investors, landowners, tribal governments, and public and private entities in navigating the legal and regulatory processes required to entitle and develop real estate projects across California. The firm provides integrated legal and land use planning services from early due diligence and entitlement strategy through environmental review, agency approvals and project implementation. Procopio’s Land Use and Environmental team integrates land use, environmental, real estate and litigation capabilities to address the issues that arise in complex development projects. Attorneys regularly advise on zoning and general plan amendments, development agreements, subdivisions, infrastructure arrangements and compliance with the California Environmental Quality Act (CEQA), including defending project approvals when challenged. artigo.texto: When will social distancing end? The unfortunate truth is that we were already socially distant, and we were already suffering for it. Data Centers and the Liberal State A liberal state does not distribute privileges or impose burdens according to popularity. Yet in recent years, data centers have been alternately privileged and burdened. When they were popular because of their promise of jobs and growth, states showered them with tax breaks. Now that they have become unpopular because of growing recognition of their demand for electricity and water, states and localities have rushed to impose peculiar regulations or even moratoriums on their construction. Recently, New York State provided a prime example of how data center opponents can go too far with its selective moratorium on their construction. It pauses certain state permits for building or expanding data centers that can consume 50 megawatts or more, pending a special environmental review. At the same time, it exempts facilities primarily devoted to other activities, such as manufacturing and health care, even if they have the same electrical demand. But why should the same demands on electricity and water be disfavored when they support politically unpopular activities and accepted when they support politically popular ones? Exemptions should reflect only demonstrable differences in harm, not the political connections or popularity of those receiving them. This issue differs somewhat from simple NIMBYism, a political tendency that generally wants to stop or slow down all construction in the interests of incumbent homeowners or businesses, as discussed in the latest Law & Liberty Forum. The focus here is on targeting particular enterprises. An enterprise’s demand for resources is not, by itself, evidence of market failure that the state needs to correct. Indeed, the market allocates resources to those willing to pay for them. If the poor need subsidies, they should be supported through taxation, not by special regulations that prevent profitable activity. Enterprises should be allowed to build under neutral rules. A liberal state protects the market economy because it reflects the voluntary choices of millions of its citizens. Of course, data centers, like other enterprises, might harm others by imposing externalities like noise and pollution on their neighbors. But neutral laws can handle these effects too. There is no need to single out data centers for special regulation or a moratorium. One virtue of common-law torts is that they apply equally to all polluters and noisemakers. If these restraints are thought too weak, other laws can supplement them, such as permit requirements. The key is to apply all the laws based on common conditions. The way regulation works should also give pause to supporters of New York-style policies. Utility regulations can allow the costs of new infrastructure to be passed on to all customers, effectively shifting some of the cost of serving a new customer onto existing customers. Higher market prices caused by additional demand are not themselves a subsidy; making existing customers pay for facilities built to serve a new business is. Data centers should pay the costs attributable to serving them, rather than shift those costs or investment risks onto captive customers. A well-known solution in utility rate regulation is to require businesses to pay the cost of new dedicated infrastructure. But this requirement should apply regardless of the business’s identity. The solution again is classical liberalism’s insistence on neutral laws. These principles should address the specific complaints against data centers. They do increase demand for water, but the resulting price changes are the market at work. If new infrastructure is needed, data center businesses can pay for it or construct it themselves. While data centers may need water during periods of peak demand, when it costs more to supply, appropriate metering and rates that are sensitive to time allow extra charges to reflect that timing. If water is not now correctly priced at times of such demand, that is the reform needed. Correct pricing will encourage new supply, such as reclaimed water, as well as better cooling systems. The answer is much the same with electricity. Infrastructure costs should be allocated according to the demands that they create and the benefits they provide. Neutrality does not require identical treatment of enterprises that impose different costs. A customer requiring a substation for their own use should make infrastructure payments that a household does not. But the relevant distinction is the burden imposed, not the business’s identity. Making an enterprise bear its costs is not discrimination. Higher prices should prompt new ways to increase supply. In many localities, excessive government regulation is one of the biggest constraints. If localities streamline permitting for new transmission, everyone can benefit from greater supply that brings down rates. Georgia Power recently announced that its contracts with new large users, including data centers, are expected to lower residential electricity costs beginning in 2029. Some data centers cause noise pollution, and a Virginia audit in 2024 on the issue suggests that continuous low-frequency noise is not subject to sufficient regulation. The solution is more comprehensive noise regulation that data centers, like everyone else, must follow. Federal and state law can address air pollution and carbon emissions if they are considered harmful. Those laws should also be applied neutrally to data centers. More generally, opponents of data centers should be challenged to identify externalities that existing law does not address. Those externalities can then be debated as a general matter rather than by focusing on data centers. The liberal state should be as neutral in its privileges as in its regulations. artigo.texto: - Geely's system took just 4 minutes and 30 seconds to charge from 10% to 70% in real-world tests, beating BYD's 5 minutes. - The fifth-generation Geely Smart Charging Station delivers peak power of 2,250 kW, above the 1,500-kW flash charger BYD unveiled in March. Geely Auto (HKEX: 0175) has unveiled a new generation of AI (artificial intelligence)-powered charging technology, delivering a direct response to BYD's (HKEX: 1211) push in the ultra-fast charging sector. The Chinese automaker launched the Geely Smart Charging technology in Ningbo on Wednesday, alongside the fifth-generation Geely Smart Charging Station. The Shendun Golden Battery, developed for ultra-fast charging and high performance, supports a peak charging rate of up to 12C, Geely said. In real-world tests, the Lynk & Co 10 and Zeekr 001 equipped with the Shendun Golden Battery charged from 10% to 70% in 4 minutes and 30 seconds, and from 10% to 97% in 8 minutes and 40 seconds. That marks the fastest production-ready charging performance to date. By comparison, BYD's second-generation Blade Battery, paired with the new-generation flash charging pile it unveiled in March, takes 5 minutes to charge from 10% to 70% and 9 minutes from 10% to 97% at normal temperatures. In a test Hongqi disclosed in July, its battery charged from 10% to 70% in just 3 minutes and 41 seconds, though no mass production timeline was given at the time. The fifth-generation Geely Smart Charging Station offers peak charging power of 2,250 kW, above the 1,500 kW maximum single-gun output of BYD's flash charging pile, which was the highest among mass-produced chargers globally when it was launched in March. At the core of the technology is Xingrui PowerMind, a smart energy AI model jointly developed with Chinese AI startup StepFun. The model coordinates the vehicle, battery, charging station, cloud, grid and energy storage system to tailor a charging strategy for each vehicle. The system can predict battery temperatures up to 30 seconds ahead and dynamically adjust charging power, aiming to keep the battery's average temperature below 55°C during charging and its peak temperature under 65°C. A supporting five-point liquid cooling system covers the entire charging chain, from the station's energy storage battery, charging pile, cable and charging port to the battery pack, which Geely said is an industry first. To address concerns that fast charging shortens battery life, Geely introduced lithium-ion pulse restoration technology, which uses micro-pulse currents to reactivate lithium ions accumulated at the negative electrode. Combined with AI charging management, the technology can extend battery cycle life by up to 20%, the company said. The next-generation Ultra Short Blade Battery, aimed at affordable models, uses Geely's in-house laser welding technology to cut heat during charging by 10% while raising the peak charging rate to 6C. Competition in China's EV market remains intense, with automakers vying for buyers on smart driving, range and ultra-fast charging. BYD has been the most aggressive driver of the flash charging race. BYD said earlier today that it will open its 2,000th highway flash charging station in China on September 24. As of August 28, the company had built 10,000 flash charging stations and reiterated its target of 20,000 by the end of the year. Battery maker Sunwoda last week unveiled a flash charging battery solution with charging metrics matching BYD's, and plans to build 10,000 megawatt-level flash charging stations by the end of 2027.

artigo.texto: O Grupo FonNet, especializado em equipamentos e infraestrutura de telecom e data centers, anunciou nesta quinta-feira, 24, o lançamento da AIKS, subsidiária dedicada a soluções com base em Inteligência Artificial (IA). A nova empresa nasce com operação independente e mira negócios com operadoras de telecomunicações, provedores de serviços de Internet (ISPs), data centers e ambientes corporativos. A AIKS vai oferecer serviços gerenciados de TI, desenvolvimento de software, soluções de IA, entre outras ferramentas de coleta e organização de dados operacionais. A empresa também vai atuar na vertical de observabilidade. A operação será lançada, formalmente, no Futurecom 2026, evento que acontecerá em São Paulo entre os dias 6 e 8 de outubro. Arthur Filgueira, CEO da FonNet, vai acumular o cargo de presidente da AIKS. A nova empresa também terá Emerson Sampaio no cargo de diretor de Tecnologia. O quadro funcional ainda inclui uma equipe multidisciplinar formada por profissionais de engenharia, arquitetura de Tecnologia da Informação e Comunicação (TIC), desenvolvimento de software, segurança cibernética, suporte e negócios. Em comunicado, a AIKS afirma que tem o objetivo de reduzir o retrabalho e melhorar a prontidão das equipes a partir de soluções capazes de identificar e corrigir falhas, sem a necessidade de substituição imediata dos sistemas atualmente em uso pelos clientes. Ou seja, as soluções podem funcionar em paralelo à infraestrutura existente. "As empresas ampliaram a quantidade de ferramentas e dados disponíveis, mas isso nem sempre significou uma capacidade maior de decisão. A AIKS vem para conectar essas informações, preservar os investimentos já realizados e ajudar as equipes a evoluir a operação de forma gradual e mensurável", afirma Filgueira.
